requirement: Implement an Anthropic message streaming handler that safely manages stream context lifecycle, records text chunks, detects token limit truncation, and handles stream errors.
skeleton: AnthropicStreamHandler with collect_stream and stream_text_chunks methods returning StreamSummary dataclass.
caption: An Anthropic-style message streaming handler written against an injected client, in the standard library with a frozen dataclass and no third-party imports, that keeps every stream inside its context manager so the connection is always closed. StreamSummary holds the joined text, the stop reason, an is_truncated flag, and the chunk count. collect_stream(model, max_tokens, messages) uses a Claude Sonnet model name by default and max_tokens defaulting to 1024, and raises ValueError reporting that messages must not be empty before opening any stream. It opens client.messages.stream with those arguments in a with block, appends every piece of stream.text_stream to a list, and, while still inside the block, calls get_final_message and reads its stop_reason, falling back to end_turn when it is missing. The summary is truncated only when the stop reason is max_tokens, so a normal end_turn completion is never reported as cut off. The summary is built and returned from inside the block, and leaving the block closes the stream. stream_text_chunks applies the same empty-message check and is a generator that opens the stream in a with block and yields each text chunk, so the stream closes when iteration finishes. The fixture asserts that two chunks produce the text Part 1 Part 2 with stop reason end_turn, not truncated, and a closed stream; that a max_tokens stop reason is reported as truncated; that empty messages raise ValueError for both methods; that the stream is opened with max_tokens 1024 by default; that the chunk count is 2; and that the generator yields A, B, and C and leaves the stream closed.

plan.intent: Consume a message stream entirely inside its context manager
constraints: Empty messages raise ValueError before any stream opens
Text chunks and the final stop reason are read inside the with block
A missing stop reason falls back to end_turn
Only a max_tokens stop reason marks the result truncated
The generator variant closes the stream when iteration ends

rationale.teaches: Streaming through the messages.stream context manager, reading the final message inside it, flagging max_tokens as truncation, refusing empty messages, and defaulting max_tokens to 1024.
rationale.why: A stream used outside its context manager still yields text, but its connection is never closed. The fixture uses a fake stream that records enter and exit and reports stop_reason.

ops.docstring: Consume Anthropic message streams inside their context manager.

ops.source:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StreamSummary:
    """Collected text and stop metadata of one finished stream."""

    text: str
    stop_reason: str
    is_truncated: bool
    chunk_count: int

class AnthropicStreamHandler:
    """Stream Anthropic messages while keeping each stream's lifetime scoped."""

    def __init__(self, client: Any) -> None:
        self.client = client

    def collect_stream(
        self,
        model: str = "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
        max_tokens: int = 1024,
        messages: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None,
    ) -> StreamSummary:
        """Drain one stream and summarise its text, stop reason, and truncation."""
        if not messages:
            raise ValueError("messages must not be empty")

        accumulated: list[str] = []
        with self.client.messages.stream(
            model=model,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=messages,
        ) as stream:
            for text_chunk in stream.text_stream:
                accumulated.append(text_chunk)

            final_message = stream.get_final_message()
            stop_reason = getattr(final_message, "stop_reason", None) or "end_turn"
            is_truncated = stop_reason == "max_tokens"

            return StreamSummary(
                text="".join(accumulated),
                stop_reason=stop_reason,
                is_truncated=is_truncated,
                chunk_count=len(accumulated),
            )

    def stream_text_chunks(
        self,
        model: str = "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
        max_tokens: int = 1024,
        messages: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None,
    ) -> Iterator[str]:
        """Yield text chunks while the underlying stream stays open."""
        if not messages:
            raise ValueError("messages must not be empty")

        with self.client.messages.stream(
            model=model,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=messages,
        ) as stream:
            yield from stream.text_stream

candidates.why_wrong: The stream is used outside its context manager, so the connection is never closed after the final message.
end_turn is flagged as truncation, so every normal completion is reported as truncated and real truncation is not.
Empty message lists are sent to the API, so the error surfaces from the client instead of as a ValueError.
max_tokens defaults to 100, so a normal response is truncated by default.
get_final_message is called after leaving the context, so the stop reason is read from a closed stream.
